data.description:
# Design experiment: validate session compaction gains without quality loss

Phase 2 of the compaction evaluation (previously LP-0MSG9PGOP009X2F2, since
deleted). Design a controlled experiment proving that compacting session
history (to fit under the routing clamp) and serving locally yields the
gains estimated in the log study (**now delivered as F1/F2 evidence:
LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B distribution analysis and LP-0MTC8A2UB0040NKQ
correlation** — see `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/`) **without
degrading output quality**.

Times two-tier scheme (epic LP-0MTCW79RR000LFMJ): this experiment's outcome
**gates Tier 1 enforcement** (proxy-side proactive compaction,
LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD). Tier 2 (hard cap + cheap gate, LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S)
is a routing-level safety net and does not depend on this experiment.

## User Story

As an operator, I want evidence that compacted-local responses are not worse
than uncompacted-remote responses on real tasks, so I can switch
over-clamp sessions to compact-and-serve-local with confidence.

## Experiment design requirements

- **Task suite**: representative real tasks drawn from logged sessions (or a
  synthetic suite mirroring them) — code editing, multi-file refactors, Q&A
  over long documents, agent tool-call loops. Must include tasks where long
  context matters (the risky population).
- **Conditions** (same tasks, three arms where feasible):
  - A: uncompacted → remote deepseek-v4-flash (current behaviour, baseline)
  - B: compacted → local Qwen3 (proposed)
  - C: uncompacted → local Qwen3 (ceiling, where the clamp allows;
    documents local capability at full context)
- **Compaction strategy**: **concrete — from the F3/F4 evaluation
  (LP-0MTC8B0BN009BMTJ / LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW)**:
  - fast profile (Strategy B): auto-truncate to ≤ 38K when > 58.3K
  - cheap profile (Strategy C): summarize → truncate to ≤ 30K when > 43K
  Arm B uses the Tier 1 machinery (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD) once implemented,
  or a manual equivalent in the interim.
- **Quality measurement**: task-completion rate, rubric-based output quality
  (or semantic-equivalence scoring vs. baseline), failure/truncation rate,
  retry rate. State the quality bar explicitly (e.g. compacted-local within
  X% of uncompacted-remote on the rubric, no increase in task failures).
- **Operational metrics**: latency (TTFT + total), local busy % change,
  remote request/token reduction, cost.
- **Go/no-go criteria**: pre-registered thresholds for quality (primary) and
  efficiency (secondary). State what would reject the approach.

## Deliverables

- Experiment design document (in a comment or repo doc referenced from this
  item) with task suite, arms, compaction strategy, metrics, sample sizes,
  and go/no-go thresholds
- List of new work items needed to implement the experiment harness, if any
- Recommendation: proceed to experiment execution (new work item) or abandon

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Design document covers arms, compaction strategy, quality metric +
      bar, operational metrics, go/no-go thresholds
- [ ] Reuses existing compaction/logging machinery (context_pressure path,
      Tier 1 warn-only dry-run); no speculative new infrastructure
- [ ] A follow-up work item for experiment execution is created if design is
      approved

## Sources

- F1 evidence: `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/distribution.md` (breach
  rates, per-mode distributions)
- F2 evidence: `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/correlation.md` (wasted
  prefill, decode collapse)
- Strategy choices: `docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md` (F4)
data.title: Design experiment: validate session compaction gains without quality loss

data.description:
Goal: Explore the bursty-fan-out workload pattern (agent sessions firing parallel requests in bursts) and recommend whether the contention queue (cheap mode, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D) caps should be tuned — vs adding slots — to improve local utilization and cut remote fallback.

Context (from proxy usage analysis, report window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52):
- Fallback events are highly bursty: 95% of the 1293 fallbacks occur within 60s of a previous fallback (median inter-arrival 4s, p90 21s) — agent sessions fanning out parallel calls.
- 37 requests queued→dispatched local and 17 fell back after the queue caps (fallback_after_queue) in-window; 120 local_dispatch_denied (active=1/2 observed at denial, below the 3-slot capacity).
- The contention queue wakes on `local_active_queries` decrement and lease release; context bypasses are never queued. Adding slots shrinks per-slot context (slots-vs-context trade-off) and raises context-bypass volume, so it is NOT a free win (see report recommendations and LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM).
- Hypothesis to test: with bursty fan-out, queue depth/wait caps (contention_queue_max_wait_seconds, contention_queue_max_depth) may be the binding constraint, and tuning them (or making them mode-aware fast/cheap) may recover more local dispatch than raising slot counts.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Quantify the burst profile: distribution of concurrent local requests during bursts, queue depth observed, queue-wait durations, and how many fallbacks occurred while the contention queue was non-empty (where derivable from logs).
2. Evaluate the expected gain of raising queue caps (wait/depth) vs raising slot counts: projected additional local dispatches saved per window, with the slots-vs-context trade-off factored in.
3. Recommend concrete config changes (values for contention_queue_max_wait_seconds / contention_queue_max_depth, per-mode if warranted) with quantified expected impact and risks (latency added by queueing, remote fallback avoided).
4. Recommendation recorded as a comment on this work item; create follow-up implementation item(s) if config changes are warranted.
data.title: Explore and recommend contention-queue tuning for bursty agent fan-out: queue caps vs more slots

data.description:
Goal: Determine why 76.1% (290/381) of `local_concurrency_limit` fallback events in the 2026-08-28/29 24h window fired while llama-server was generating nothing (0 active local streams), and evaluate concrete ways to reduce local per-request processing time.

Context (from proxy usage analysis, report window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52):
- 1293 fallback events; 52.5% (679) fired with 0 active local streams; 99.1% with ≤2 of 3 fast slots.
- `local_concurrency_limit` (381 events, 29.5% of fallbacks) compares the proxy's `local_active_queries` counter (provider.py:_get_local_concurrency_info, line ~1803) against `session_slot_pool_size`. The counter spans the whole request lifecycle at the proxy layer (prompt-eval/prefill, contention-queue waits, lease holds), not just token generation — so it can read "full" while llama-server is idle.
- `Stream started` is logged inside `stream_generator()` (router.py:1092), i.e. at first-byte time, so prompt-eval/prefill time is NOT counted in the report's busy-time metric (27.9% busy). Prefill estimate: median prompt eval ~100 tok/s vs avg-max context ~123389 tokens → potentially ~20 min prefill for the largest prompts.
- Candidate contributors to idle-time counter occupancy: (a) prefill before first token, (b) contention-queue waits (cheap mode queue policy, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D), (c) no-preemption lease hold/cooldown (router_helpers.py:_try_acquire_local_dispatch, "inactive lease (post-request cooldown) reserves its slot").

Acceptance criteria:
1. Quantified verdict: measure actual prefill time (prompt-eval seconds from llama-server eval-timing lines, total per window) vs decode/busy time, and the distribution of time between `local_active_queries` increment and `Stream started` (first-byte) where derivable; state whether prefill, queue waits, or lease holds dominate the idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` count.
2. Confirm or refute the counter-over-count hypothesis with event-level evidence (e.g. a burst of `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks during a llama-server idle stretch, with no queued work).
3. Evaluate 2-3 concrete levers to improve local processing time (e.g. prefill offloading/batching, adaptive lease timeouts, counting only generating requests toward the pool, prompt-cache positioning to raise warm-cache hit rate) with expected impact quantified from the window data.
4. Recommendation recorded as a comment on this work item with evidence, linked work items (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM etc.), and a proposed follow-up implementation item if warranted.
data.title: Investigate idle-time local_concurrency_limit fallbacks: does local_active_queries over-count busy? Evaluate improving local processing time
